page.overview:
What is Ost-in-Edhil?

Ost-in-Edhil was the capital city of the Elven realm of Eregion in the Second Age.

Ost-in-Edhil was established by the Ñoldor in SA 750, located where the river Sirannon met the Glanduin. The Elven-way was eventually constructed to the West-gate of Khazad-dûm under the shadow of the Misty Mountains, to facilitate communication and trade between the Dwarves and the Elves.

The city was ruled by Celebrimbor, founder and leader of the Gwaith-i-Mírdain and grandson of Fëanor. Here the Ñoldor created the Rings of Power with knowledge given to them by Sauron, posing as Annatar, "Giver of Gifts". When Celebrimbor discovered Sauron's plan to ensnare them, he hid the rings and did not use them ever again, refusing Sauron's demand to surrender all the others. This incited the War of the Elves and Sauron, in which Ost-in-Edhil was soon completely destroyed by Sauron's forces. Its ruins survived into the Third Age.

Three millennia later, the Fellowship of the Ring encountered the ruins of Ost-in-Edhil shortly before reaching Moria, and Legolas "heard" the stones speaking of the Elves of Eregion: "Deep they delved us, High they built us, Fair they wrought us, But they are gone."
